hypothesis: A write-and-read-registers request can write before the holding-register allocation when its write address precedes the configured mapping start. The bounds check tests mapping_address twice and never rejects a negative mapping_address_write.
evidence_source: Lines 952-953 calculate separate read and write mapping offsets. Lines 962-965 check mapping_address < 0 twice, while checking only the upper bound of the write range. Lines 978-981 subsequently index tab_registers using mapping_address_write.
input_artifact: not_available (static source review; no input artifact)
expected_behavior: An out-of-bounds write before tab_registers, potentially producing an AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow report, heap corruption, or a crash.
observed_behavior: not_available (static source review; nothing was executed)
notes: Requires a mapping with a nonzero start_registers and otherwise valid request quantities and payload length. The defect does not depend on a truncated frame or on bypassing the receive-side maximum-length check. Replace the repeated read-offset check with mapping_address_write < 0.
